To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the results of assisted reproductive technologies in Spain are better in private clinics than in public clinics.
private assisted reproduction clinics in Spain perform more cycles and transfers than public clinics, with similar or higher success rates.
public clinics perform proportionally more transfers than private clinics and the pregnancy rate is significantly higher in private clinics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of the public/private status of the assisted reproduction centres.
the influence of the different types of clinic on assisted reproduction activity, treatment patterns and clinical results.
the analysis of the activities and results obtained in the assisted reproduction centres in the period 2002- 2004, and the comparison between public and private centres.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the private clinics are more active, offer a greater range of services, perform more transfers, and achieve better clinical results than the public centres.
the public clinics are more conservative, with less elective transfer of embryos and fewer multiple-pregnancies than the private ones.
public and private clinics have different profiles, and that this is reflected in their activity and in their results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results obtained in private assisted reproduction clinics are superior to the results obtained by public clinics, although the differences are not very marked.
public clinics are more conservative and less innovative in the treatment of infertile couples.
the private clinics perform more cycles and transfers, with more embryos, with higher pregnancy and implantation rates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the public and private sectors are complementary, and that the private sector is more active in the assisted reproduction field.
public centres are not performing as many oocyte donations and preimplantational genetic diagnosis cycles as the private ones.
public clinics perform proportionally more transfers with three embryos than the clinics in the private sector, and that the pregnancy rate is lower among the former than the latter.
